correctness.rationale: The nonzero radical products land in a one-dimensional annihilator, which proves associativity. The commutator, center and radical recover an intrinsic two-dimensional quotient. The quadratic square map forces Q_target(Lv)=det(L)Q_source(v). Conversely, its alternating bilinear discrepancy can always be absorbed by a linear dual-valued shear with exactly \(q^3\) solutions, while two independent maps to the annihilator contribute \(q^4\); these \(q^7\) lifts are all invertible and account for all automorphisms. Standard nonsingular binary quadratic-form classification proves the trace criterion; the split and anisotropic similitude groups have orders \(2(q-1)^2\) and \(2(q^2-1)\). Square-zero fibers and extension parity follow by counting roots of Q. Direct finite-field checks over F2, F4, and F8, exhaustive F2 lift enumeration and a fully verified explicit F4 change of basis confirm the critical formulas. The proof, rather than the finite checks, supplies all-q quantifiers.

value.rationale: A recently classified minimal example of noncommutative central essentiality raises a natural next structural question: determine the actual automorphism groups and behavior under scalar extension. The theorem answers this for every binary finite field in a uniform, explicit way; it gives a \(q^7\) lifting mechanism rather than ad hoc small-group calculations, a contrast between two quotient orthogonal groups, and a sharp parity law showing descent failure and recovery over even-degree extensions. The exact automorphism count and lift structure are intrinsic and useful for finite ring isomorphism enumeration and symmetry calculations. Only the binary isomorphism classification and classical Arf input are known and specifically credited; the new result is not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere reinterpretation of a small finite table.
